transcript.cleaned_text: A 104-year-old woman is selling the house she has lived in since she was two years old. [1]Nancy Gifford was born months after the end of the First World War and spent 102 years living in her three-bedroom house in the Somerset Village of Street. She is now putting it on the market, having lived in it through the Second World War and the invention of television. Her family bought the house for 200 pounds in 1921. And it is now priced at some 170,000 pounds. According to the Bank of England's inflation calculator, 200 pounds in 1921 would be worth 7,750 pounds today. According to the estate agent, the house was built in 1882 and originally featured a well for the entire road. Except for some changes in the toilet and wash area, much of the house remains the same. [2]Mrs Gifford is selling the house and moving to a nursing home in nearby Glastonbury because of her health.

transcript.cleaned_text: The navy rescued a man who survived 24 days floating in the sea on a boat by eating tomato sauce and vegetable powder. [3]The man, 47, wrote the word HELP in English on the boat, which was key to his rescue. The man told authorities that his experience began in December when currents swept the sailboat out to sea while he was making repairs. To survive, the man collected rainwater with a cloth. He had to constantly remove water from the boat to prevent it from sinking. He also tried to light a fire to send a distress signal without success. Finally, a plane passed by and he signaled with a mirror. He said the navy told him that he was spotted when the plane passed again. The sailboat was abandoned at sea when the man was picked up by a nearby merchant ship. [4]He was found in good health but had lost weight.

The specific schools will be announced in the coming days, a district spokesperson said. [6]In the next three years, the district expects to enroll 3,000 fewer elementary and middle school students, it said. 3,000 students may not seem like that many students, but to a budget where you’re receiving per-pupil funding, that’s about 36 million dollars, district spokesperson Scott Bribble said. “We know that there are impacts and it’s heartbreaking and difficult work, [7]but in order for the district to stay out of debt, it’s a step that needs to be taken,” he said. transcript.cleaned_text: If US workers want to switch jobs, they’d better do it now. Last year, job switchers earned far higher wage increases than those staying in their jobs, but the gap is now closing. A three-month moving average of annual wage increases from the Atlanta Federal Reserve Bank’s wage tracker shows that US job switchers got the highest wage increase last July, when the measure touched 8.5 percent. Since then, it has gone up and down, and has been going steadily down since November. [16]The gap in wage gains between people who switched jobs and those who stayed in their jobs is now closing. On average, people who changed jobs have almost always gotten better pay raises than those who stayed, but in the past the difference was usually around one percentage point. [17]In July, though, the gap widened to 2.6 percentage points. But now wage growth is slowing down for everyone, and job switchers are getting smaller wage bumps in their new jobs. At the moment, those who change jobs get an average 7.3% raise every year, while those who stay get a 5.4% raise. That suggests the demand for workers has reached or is at least nearing its peak. [18]The labor market is likely cooling, because even a shortage of workers isn’t overcoming the historic imbalance between employers and employees in the US; the volume of income that workers take home as a proportion of what the US economy produces is still falling.

transcript.cleaned_text: Highly processed foods—the kinds made with lots of sugar, fat and salt—make up as much as sixty percent of the average American diet, [19]but a new study shows that their low price and convenience come at a cost to health. The study found that when people ate a highly processed diet, they consumed about five hundred more calories per day than they did when they ate a less processed diet. They also gained two pounds over two weeks even though both diets had the same amounts of nutrients like sugar, fat, fiber and salt. It wasn’t a shock to find highly processed foods weren’t healthy. [20]Other research has linked them to a higher risk of cancer and obesity. What was unexpected was that sugar, fat and salt didn’t seem to be what caused people to overeat. This is the first trial that demonstrates that there is something about highly processed foods independent of those nutrients that causes people to overeat. [21]The study also found that when eating a highly processed diet, people ate faster. This could be one reason why they gained more weight. Highly processed food tends to be softer, which makes it easier to chew and swallow. One theory is that if you’re eating more quickly, you’re not giving your gut enough time to signal to your brain that you’ve had enough calories and that you’re full. By the time the brain gets that signal, you’ve already overeaten.

transcript.cleaned_text: [22]Women continue to spend more time than men taking care of children and doing chores around the house. This is generally attributed to backward thinking and conservative values, but new research shows that such differences could be linked to differences in the preferences of males and females. The new study looked at how men and women were dividing work at home and why they divided it that way. [23]In general, both men and women took more responsibility for tasks they liked. For example, men liked yard care and home maintenance more than women. They leaned toward wanting primary responsibility for such tasks. The researchers stated that differences in enjoyment of household and childcare tasks matched how men and women chose to split tasks. The researchers added that there was not a single childcare task that men liked more than women. [24]Keep in mind, however, that as with any research on group differences, there were large within-group differences. The study’s authors concluded that differences in men’s and women’s time spent on childcare and household tasks do not mean dissatisfaction. [25]The authors noted that previous research revealed gender differences in attitudes towards family and career. These differences appear as early as six years old; girls that age already show more interest in helping and caring for others than boys do, and they already exhibit a greater orientation toward family versus career.

options.label: A
options.text_en: Approve criteria for closing schools with decreased funding.
options.text_zh: 通过针对经费缩减而关停学校的标准。

options.label: B
options.text_en: Enroll 3,000 fewer elementary and middle school students.
options.text_zh: 小学和中学的入学人数将减少 3,000 人。

options.label: C
options.text_en: Decide which elementary and middle schools to close.
options.text_zh: 确定要关停哪些小学和中学。

options.label: D
options.text_en: Alter its per-pupil funding policy on a rational basis.
options.text_zh: 基于合理依据修改按人头拨款政策。

questions.question_text: Why are some schools in Denver to be closed according to the district spokesperson?
questions.question_text_zh: 根据校区发言人的说法，丹佛的一些学校为什么要关闭？

options.label: A
options.text_en: To enable the district to remain competitive.
options.text_zh: 为了让校区保持竞争力。

options.label: B
options.text_en: To avoid a negative impact on its economy.
options.text_zh: 为了避免对当地经济造成负面影响。

options.label: C
options.text_en: To keep the district free of debt.

options.label: D
options.text_en: To obtain the expected funding.

questions.question_text: Why does the woman call the man?
questions.question_text_zh: 女士为什么给男士打电话？

options.label: A
options.text_en: To book tickets for a musical.
options.text_zh: 为了预定一场音乐剧的门票。

options.label: B
options.text_en: To enquire about the price of cats.

options.label: C
options.text_en: To pay for her afternoon flight to London.
options.text_zh: 为了支付她下午飞往伦敦的航班费用。

options.label: D
options.text_en: To have her personal computer repaired.
options.text_zh: 为了找人修理她的个人电脑。

questions.question_text: What do we learn about the woman's husband?
questions.question_text_zh: 关于女士的丈夫，我们可以了解什么？

options.label: A
options.text_en: He frequents the Lion Theatre.

options.label: B
options.text_en: He knows how to sell things well.
options.text_zh: 他了解如何更好地卖东西。

options.label: C
options.text_en: He is a computer science expert.

options.label: D
options.text_en: He is away on a business trip.

questions.question_text: What does the man say about the tickets at the front?
questions.question_text_zh: 关于前排的票，男士提到了什么？

options.label: A
options.text_en: They are sold at a discount.

options.label: B
options.text_en: They are in low demand.

options.label: C
options.text_en: They are no longer available.

options.label: D
options.text_en: They are not too expensive.

questions.question_text: What does the woman say she is scared of?
questions.question_text_zh: 女士说她害怕什么？

options.label: A
options.text_en: Heights.

options.label: B
options.text_en: Circus.

options.label: C
options.text_en: Wild animals.

options.label: D
options.text_en: Dark nights.

questions.question_text: Why hasn't the man answered the woman's text messages lately?
questions.question_text_zh: 这位男士最近为什么没有回复这位女士的短信？

options.label: A
options.text_en: He finds it bothersome to reply.
options.text_zh: 他发现回复消息很麻烦。

options.label: B
options.text_en: He has switched off his phone.

options.label: C
options.text_en: He hasn't got the time to text back.

options.label: D
options.text_en: He doesn't know how to respond.

questions.question_text: What was the man shocked to realize after he downloaded the app?
questions.question_text_zh: 这位男士下载了应用之后，震惊地意识到了什么？

options.label: A
options.text_en: His lack of sufficient sleep at night.

options.label: B
options.text_en: His addiction to mobile phone games.

options.label: C
options.text_en: His excessive use of the mobile phone.

options.label: D
options.text_en: His high frequency of surfing the net.

questions.question_text: What did the man spend much time doing with his phone?
questions.question_text_zh: 男士在手机上花费很多时间做什么？

options.label: A
options.text_en: Shopping online and paying for his purchases.

options.label: B
options.text_en: Communicating with friends on social media.
options.text_zh: 在社交媒体上与朋友交流。

options.label: C
options.text_en: Exploring whatever content to his liking.

options.label: D
options.text_en: Sharing and posting pictures and videos.
options.text_zh: 分享并发布图片和视频。

questions.question_text: Why does the woman say she has to use her mobile phone?
questions.question_text_zh: 女士为什么说她不得不使用手机？

options.label: A
options.text_en: She prefers chatting with others online to meeting them.
options.text_zh: 相比线下见面，她更喜欢在线上和别人聊天。

options.label: B
options.text_en: There are few physical stores near where she lives.
options.text_zh: 她住的地方附近实体店很少。

options.label: C
options.text_en: Ordering meals online is a great convenience to her.
options.text_zh: 线上点餐对她来说十分方便。

options.label: D
options.text_en: She needs to talk with her friends and family far away.
options.text_zh: 她需要与远方的朋友和家人聊天。

questions.question_text: What does the passage say about the gap in wage gains between job switchers and those who stay in their jobs?
questions.question_text_zh: 关于跳槽者和留职者之间的薪资增长差距，篇章表述了什么？

options.label: A
options.text_en: It is now narrowing.

options.label: B
options.text_en: It keeps increasing.

options.label: C
options.text_en: It has remained huge.

options.label: D
options.text_en: It will soon disappear.

questions.question_text: What do we learn about wage growth now?
questions.question_text_zh: 我们现在对薪资增长有什么了解？

options.label: A
options.text_en: It is fluctuating between 5-7%.

options.label: B
options.text_en: It is slowing down for everyone.
options.text_zh: 所有人的薪资增长都在放缓。

options.label: C
options.text_en: It is faster for those who stay in their jobs.

options.label: D
options.text_en: It is inadequate for dealing with inflation.

questions.question_text: What is the labor market likely doing according to the passage?
questions.question_text_zh: 根据篇章内容，劳动力市场可能有什么变化？

options.label: A
options.text_en: Booming.

options.label: B
options.text_en: Stabilizing.

options.label: C
options.text_en: Struggling.

options.label: D
options.text_en: Cooling.

questions.question_text: What does a new study show about highly processed foods?
questions.question_text_zh: 一项新研究对深加工食品有何发现？

options.label: A
options.text_en: They have smaller amounts of nutrients than unprocessed diets.
options.text_zh: 与未加工食品相比，它们的营养成分含量较低。

options.label: B
options.text_en: Their contribution to calorie consumption is hard to determine.
options.text_zh: 难以判定它们对热量摄入的影响。

options.label: C
options.text_en: They account for nearly half of the average American diet.
options.text_zh: 它们约占普通美国人日常饮食的一半。

options.label: D
options.text_en: Their low price and convenience negatively impact health.
options.text_zh: 它们低廉的价格和便捷性会对健康产生负面影响。

questions.question_text: What are highly processed foods linked to according to other research?
questions.question_text_zh: 其他研究将深加工食品与什么联系在一起？

options.label: A
options.text_en: A strong desire to overeat.

options.label: B
options.text_en: A lack of nutrients like fiber.
options.text_zh: 缺乏像膳食纤维这样的营养物质。

options.label: C
options.text_en: A higher risk of cancer and obesity.

options.label: D
options.text_en: A greater intake of sugar and salt.

questions.question_text: What do people tend to do when eating highly processed foods?
questions.question_text_zh: 人们在食用深加工食品时倾向于做什么？

options.label: A
options.text_en: Eat more quickly.

options.label: B
options.text_en: Feel full sooner.

options.label: C
options.text_en: Chew thoroughly.

options.label: D
options.text_en: Swallow bit by bit.

questions.question_text: How do people generally account for differences between men and women in the amount of time spent on housework?
questions.question_text_zh: 人们通常如何解释男女在做家务时间上的差异？

options.label: A
options.text_en: By attributing them to current cultural influences.
options.text_zh: 将其归因于当前的文化影响。

options.label: B
options.text_en: By attributing them to conservative thinking.

options.label: C
options.text_en: In terms of new genetic findings.

options.label: D
options.text_en: In terms of personal preferences.

questions.question_text: What did men lean toward doing according to the new study?
questions.question_text_zh: 根据这项新研究，男性倾向于做什么？

options.label: A
options.text_en: Sharing with women the chores they see necessary.
options.text_zh: 与女性分担他们认为必要的家务。

options.label: B
options.text_en: Dividing housework that is demanding for women.
options.text_zh: 分担对女性来说繁重的家务。

options.label: C
options.text_en: Performing household tasks that they enjoy.

options.label: D
options.text_en: Doing tasks that are physically challenging.
options.text_zh: 做体力上具有挑战性的家务。

questions.question_text: What should we keep in mind as regards any research on group differences?
questions.question_text_zh: 针对任何有关群体差异的研究，我们应记住什么？

options.label: A
options.text_en: The large within-group differences.
options.text_zh: 群体内部存在较大差异。

options.label: B
options.text_en: The great similarities across groups.

options.label: C
options.text_en: The researchers' subjective biases.

options.label: D
options.text_en: The noticeable overgeneralizations.

questions.question_text: What did previous research reveal about gender differences in attitudes toward family and career?
questions.question_text_zh: 以往的研究揭示了对待家庭和事业的态度存在怎样的性别差异？

options.label: A
options.text_en: They seem to be universal.

options.label: B
options.text_en: They impact people's whole life.

options.label: C
options.text_en: They shape one's role in society.
options.text_zh: 它们塑造了个人在社会中的角色。

options.label: D
options.text_en: They appear at an early age.
options.text_zh: 它们在年纪小的时候就出现了。
